title: Three Drugs, One Gauge
endLine: Lower liver ER cholesterol any way, and receptors tend to rise.

scenes.tts: A liver cell reads cholesterol in its E R membrane. When the reading falls, it makes more L D L receptors. Now meet three drugs. A statin blocks the cell's own making line. The other two act in the gut. How can a drug in the gut change receptors in the liver?
scenes.narration: A liver cell reads cholesterol in its ER membrane. When the reading falls, it makes more LDL receptors. Now meet three drugs. A statin blocks the cell's own making line. The other two act in the gut. How can a drug in the gut change receptors in the liver?
scenes.caption: A liver cell reads cholesterol in its ER membrane. When the reading falls, it makes more LDL receptors. Now meet three drugs. A statin blocks the cell's own making line. The other two act in the gut. How can a drug in the gut change receptors in the liver?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's world and colour map without a reset. One large schematic liver-cell cross-section fills the upper two-thirds of the frame: blood channel along its left edge carrying the same bright LDL circles, receptor cups on the surface, the ER ribbon with its cholesterol gauge (a needle dial) at the centre, the lower synthesis pipe with its HMG-CoA reductase valve, GOLD cholesterol tokens flowing into the ER pool. New for this film: a horizontal band across the bottom third labelled 'gut', with slow peristaltic ripples, joined to the liver cell by one short pipe labelled 'from gut' that carries a few GOLD tokens upward. A small 'schematic' tag sits bottom right all film. During the link-back, the gauge needle dips and two extra receptor cups pop onto the surface, then retract to the starting count. On 'three drugs', three labelled pills drop in: RED 'statin' lands on the reductase valve (the first film's red stop); ORANGE 'ezetimibe' and PURPLE 'resin' land in the gut band. On the question, a dotted white arc draws from the two gut pills up to the receptor cups, and a large question mark sits on the arc. LDL circles keep drifting in the blood and the gut keeps rippling throughout.
Title 'Three Drugs, One Gauge' fades in across the middle for 2 s while the question mark fades. LDL circles keep drifting, gut ripples continue, GOLD tokens keep flowing into the ER pool.

scenes.tts: Start with the drug from before. A statin blocks H M G coenzyme A reductase, the main throttle. Less new cholesterol reaches the E R, so the gauge reads low.
scenes.narration: Start with the drug from before. A statin blocks HMG-CoA reductase, the main throttle. Less new cholesterol reaches the ER, so the gauge reads low.
scenes.caption: Start with the drug from before. A statin blocks HMG-CoA reductase, the main throttle. Less new cholesterol reaches the ER, so the gauge reads low.
scenes.visual: Camera eases toward the lower synthesis pipe; the gut band stays visible but dimmed. The RED statin stop slides fully into the reductase valve; the stream of GOLD tokens leaving the valve thins to a trickle while upstream blocks queue. On 'gauge reads low', the gauge needle swings down about one third of its range (schematic, no numbers) and a small RED tick marks 'statin' on the dial at that position. The trickle keeps moving.

scenes.tts: Cholesterol also reaches the liver from the gut. Ezetimibe blocks cholesterol absorption, so less arrives by that route. A different door, yet the E R reading drops again.
scenes.narration: Cholesterol also reaches the liver from the gut. Ezetimibe blocks cholesterol absorption, so less arrives by that route. A different door, yet the ER reading drops again.
scenes.caption: Cholesterol also reaches the liver from the gut. Ezetimibe blocks cholesterol absorption, so less arrives by that route. A different door, yet the ER reading drops again.
scenes.visual: Camera pans down to the gut band and the 'from gut' pipe; the liver cell stays in frame above. GOLD tokens rise from the gut through the pipe into the liver cell's ER pool. On 'Ezetimibe blocks', the ORANGE pill settles at the pipe's gut opening as a labelled orange gate, and most GOLD tokens bounce off it and drift on along the gut; only a few pass. On 'the ER reading drops', the gauge needle swings down again and an ORANGE tick labelled 'ezetimibe' appears on the dial. The statin is lifted out first so each drug is shown on its own (the red tick stays as a faint mark).

scenes.tts: The third drug is a bile-acid resin. The liver makes bile acids from its own cholesterol. The resin traps bile acids in the gut. Predict: what happens to cholesterol in the liver cell's E R?
scenes.narration: The third drug is a bile-acid resin. The liver makes bile acids from its own cholesterol. The resin traps bile acids in the gut. Predict: what happens to cholesterol in the liver cell's ER?
scenes.caption: The third drug is a bile-acid resin. The liver makes bile acids from its own cholesterol. The resin traps bile acids in the gut. Predict: what happens to cholesterol in the liver cell's ER?
scenes.visual: The orange gate lifts away. A second, thin outflow appears from the liver cell down to the gut, labelled 'bile acids'. On 'makes bile acids from its own cholesterol', a GOLD token in the ER pool turns into a GREEN droplet and slides down that outflow into the gut. On 'traps bile acids', the PURPLE pill opens into a purple mesh in the gut labelled 'resin', and GREEN droplets stick to it instead of rising back toward the liver, and are carried out along the gut. Question card at top in white: 'ER cholesterol?' with three compact choices: 'rises', 'falls', 'no change'. Do not move the gauge needle yet; return it to its resting position before the card appears.

Thinking pause. The question card and its three choices stay. GREEN droplets keep collecting in the purple mesh, the gut keeps rippling, LDL circles drift in the blood. The gauge needle holds still at rest; reveal no answer.

scenes.tts: It falls. With bile acids trapped in the gut, the liver turns more of its own cholesterol into new bile acids. So E R cholesterol drops.
scenes.narration: It falls. With bile acids trapped in the gut, the liver turns more of its own cholesterol into new bile acids. So ER cholesterol drops.
scenes.caption: It falls. With bile acids trapped in the gut, the liver turns more of its own cholesterol into new bile acids. So ER cholesterol drops.
scenes.visual: Highlight 'falls' and dissolve the card. In the liver cell, GOLD tokens in the ER pool turn into GREEN droplets faster and stream down the bile-acid outflow; the GOLD pool visibly shrinks. On 'ER cholesterol drops', the gauge needle swings down and a PURPLE tick labelled 'resin' joins the red and orange ticks on the dial, all three near the same low position (schematic).

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. Any drug that lowers cholesterol in the liver cell's E R tends to raise L D L receptors. The gauge reads the level, not where the shortage began.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. Any drug that lowers cholesterol in the liver cell's ER tends to raise LDL receptors. The gauge reads the level, not where the shortage began.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. Any drug that lowers cholesterol in the liver cell's ER tends to raise LDL receptors. The gauge reads the level, not where the shortage began.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world. The three drug pills sit at their sites at once: RED on the reductase valve, ORANGE at the gut pipe, PURPLE mesh in the gut. Three coloured arrows run from them into the single ER gauge and merge into one white arrow at the needle. On 'tends to raise LDL receptors', the needle sits low and the receptor-cup row on the surface begins to lengthen. On 'not where the shortage began', the three coloured arrows fade and only the white arrow into the gauge remains.

scenes.tts: Freed S R E B P two turns on the L D L receptor gene. Liver cells carry most of the body's L D L receptors. More of them at the surface pull more L D L from the blood. This takes hours, because the gauge changes how much protein is made.
scenes.narration: Freed SREBP-2 turns on the LDL-receptor gene. Liver cells carry most of the body's LDL receptors. More of them at the surface pull more LDL from the blood. This takes hours, because the gauge changes how much protein is made.
scenes.caption: Freed SREBP-2 turns on the LDL-receptor gene. Liver cells carry most of the body's LDL receptors. More of them at the surface pull more LDL from the blood. This takes hours, because the gauge changes how much protein is made.
scenes.visual: Reuse the first film's cartoon: SCAP carries SREBP-2 from the ER to a small Golgi stack, where a piece labelled 'active SREBP-2' is cut free and moves into the nucleus (a circle at the cell's right). An arrow from the nucleus to the surface; the receptor-cup row grows from three cups to eight. LDL circles in the blood channel are caught by the cups and pulled inside more often; a small blood-LDL meter beside the channel falls (schematic, no numbers). Keep the capture loop running through the scene. On 'This takes hours', a small clock icon beside the nucleus sweeps once (schematic).

scenes.tts: But the same switch turns on one more gene. It makes P C S K nine, a protein the cell secretes. P C S K nine binds the L D L receptor and sends it to the lysosome to be destroyed.
scenes.narration: But the same switch turns on one more gene. It makes PCSK9, a protein the cell secretes. PCSK9 binds the LDL receptor and sends it to the lysosome to be destroyed.
scenes.caption: But the same switch turns on one more gene. It makes PCSK9, a protein the cell secretes. PCSK9 binds the LDL receptor and sends it to the lysosome to be destroyed.
scenes.visual: A second arrow leaves the nucleus. MAGENTA tags labelled 'PCSK9' exit the cell into the blood channel. Show a receptor cup collecting LDL and being taken inside in a pocket; one MAGENTA tag clips onto that receptor. Inside the cell, a dark-red round compartment labelled 'lysosome' appears near the nucleus. On 'sends it to the lysosome', the tagged cup is carried into the lysosome and fades. Nothing molecular; tags and cups are cartoons.

scenes.tts: Fewer receptors return to the surface. So a statin raises P C S K nine along with the receptors, and gives back part of its gain. The gauge brakes its own answer.
scenes.narration: Fewer receptors return to the surface. So a statin raises PCSK9 along with the receptors, and gives back part of its gain. The gauge brakes its own answer.
scenes.caption: Fewer receptors return to the surface. So a statin raises PCSK9 along with the receptors, and gives back part of its gain. The gauge brakes its own answer.
scenes.visual: Bring the RED statin stop back onto the reductase valve and hold the gauge low. The receptor row, now eight cups, loses two as MAGENTA tags carry them to the lysosome (six remain). The blood-LDL meter drifts back up a little, but stays below where it started (schematic). On 'brakes its own answer', the two arrows from the nucleus (one to receptors, one to PCSK9) pulse together.

scenes.tts: Three drugs, three doors: the making line, absorption, and the bile-acid drain. Each one empties the same E R pool. Whatever drains it, the liver tends to answer the same way, with more receptors at its surface.
scenes.narration: Three drugs, three doors: the making line, absorption, and the bile-acid drain. Each one lowers the same ER pool. Whatever drains it, the liver tends to answer the same way, with more receptors at its surface.
scenes.caption: Three drugs, three doors: the making line, absorption, and the bile-acid drain. Each one lowers the same ER pool. Whatever drains it, the liver tends to answer the same way, with more receptors at its surface.
scenes.visual: Replay as one continuous movement in the carried world. On 'the making line', the RED stop pulses on the valve; on 'absorption', the ORANGE gate pulses at the gut pipe; on 'the bile-acid drain', the PURPLE mesh pulses with GREEN droplets on it. On 'the same ER pool', GOLD tokens drain from the pool and the needle falls. On 'more receptors', the cup row lengthens and LDL circles stream inside. MAGENTA tags stay faintly visible in the blood; add no new label.

House end card over the dimmed but still moving world (LDL circles drifting, gut rippling, gauge needle low). Large white text, centred: 'Lower liver ER cholesterol any way, and receptors tend to rise.' Hex waves once beneath it. Keep every element inside the safe frame; the line is the dominant object.
